paragraflar: Application no. 13566/24 Okan AYDAY against Türkiye lodged on 5 April 2024 communicated on 28 October 2026
The application concerns the applicant’s inability to talk to his lawyer on the telephone in prison.

The applicant was detained in Tekirdağ T‑type Prison pending the appeal proceedings following his conviction for attempting to overthrow the constitutional order. He submitted a petition to the prison administration requesting permission to speak by telephone to his lawyer, who lived in Ankara, where the criminal proceedings against him had been conducted.

On 1 December 2022 the prison administration rejected the applicant’s request pursuant to section 74 of the Regulation on the Management of Prisons and the Execution of Sentences and Preventive Measures, which provides that a convicted prisoner may make telephone calls only to his or her spouse, relatives of up to the fourth degree and legal guardians.

The applicant objected to the prison administration’s decision before the enforcement judge. He stated that there were more than ten sets of proceedings regarding him pending before the domestic courts and that he had two applications pending before the European Court of Human Rights. Accordingly, it was difficult for him and his lawyer to exchange on all these proceedings through written correspondence. Moreover, he would not be able to bear the financial burden of regularly inviting his lawyer to visit him in Tekirdağ for meetings in prison.

The applicant further submitted that, in its judgment in Mehmet Koray Eryaşa (no. 2013/6693, 16 April 2015), the Constitutional Court had held that the ability of an applicant who was detained pending appeal against a conviction to make telephone calls to his lawyer could not be restricted in accordance with section 114 of Law no. 5275 on the Enforcement of Sentences and Preventive Measures, which prohibits any interference with a detainee’s correspondence with his lawyer.
On 15 December 2022 the enforcement judge dismissed the applicant’s complaint, finding the prison administration’s decision to be in accordance with the law and procedure.
On 10 January 2023 the Assize Court rejected the applicant’s objection to that decision.

On 19 March 2024 the Constitutional Court declared the applicant’s complaints under Articles 8 and 13 of the Convention inadmissible, referring to its judgment in Sinan Gül (no. 2023/6747, 19 March 2024), which concerned the inability of a convicted person, following a final conviction, to make telephone calls in prison.
Relying on Article 8 of the Convention, the applicant complains about his inability to make telephone calls to his lawyer while in prison.

1. Has there been an interference with the applicant’s rights under Article 8 § 1 of the Convention, on account of his inability to talk to his lawyer on the telephone in prison (see Campbell v. the United Kingdom, 25 March 1992, §§ 46 and 50, Series A no. 233, and Altay v. Turkey (no. 2), no. 11236/09, § 49, 9 April 2019)?

2. If so, was that interference in accordance with the law and necessary in terms of Article 8 § 2 of the Convention (see Canavcı and Others v. Türkiye, nos. 24074/19 and 2 others, §§ 93-108, 14 November 2023; and Danilevich v. Russia, no. 31469/08, §§ 45, 48, 50 and 63, 19 October 2021)?
